review.summary: SWE-agent makes a substantial, practically relevant contribution by treating the agent-computer interface as a design variable for repository-level software engineering. Its custom search, editing, feedback, and context-management tools are evaluated on SWE-bench and supported by interface ablations, showing notable gains over the tested shell-only and retrieval baselines. The evidence is meaningful but bounded to two leading closed models and the benchmark/setup described; the paper also reports persistent inefficient agent behavior.

observations.claim: The paper articulates a coherent ACI design methodology, emphasizing simplicity, efficient actions, informative feedback, and guardrails.
The reported benchmark results show a clear improvement over the tested baselines, with interface ablations supporting the claim that design choices matter.
The main reported results are restricted to two leading models; transfer of the ACI findings to other models is not established by the evaluated results described here.
observations.quote: All results, ablations, and analysis are based on two leading LMs

observations.claim: The behavioral analysis identifies a potentially important persistence failure: agents often continue a routine without recognizing dead ends or changing approach.
observations.quote: agents rarely deviate from this pattern but they rarely recognize dead ends or reset their problem solving approach.

unresolved_questions: How well do the ACI principles and performance gains transfer to other model families, open models, or substantially different software engineering tasks?
Which individual ACI components contribute most reliably across repositories and tasks, beyond the reported Lite ablations?

Inspection covered pages 1–9, including the main design, results, and discussion, but not pages 10–25 (including appendices); implementation details and any further caveats or analyses there remain unassessed.
